about: Capability statement of the Hexplain reference implementation (hexplain-tools), per conformance class of the Processing Model. It is the machine-readable source of the informative reference-implementation notes in specification/processing/index.html (tools/test_reference_claims.py checks them against it), and the engine's README states the same claims. It is a statement of what the implementation claims, not evidence that it conforms; the engine's own test suites and the conformance corpus are that evidence.

implementation.name: hexplain-tools
implementation.readme: The engine README's conformance section mirrors this file; a change here is made there in the same release.

tree-documents.note: XML and JSON, parsed and lifted. Inside a tree document, the byte-level clauses a field located by path cannot carry are refused with Unsupported feature, as the Processing Model allows.

grouped-headers.note: On bddo:KeyValueHeader containers, all three grouping styles.

nested-profiles.note: Refused with Unsupported feature when the bundle profile is loaded.

chunked-cell-access.note: Chunk declarations are accepted and the field's bytes are read; addressing a cell through the chunk table raises Unsupported feature.

chunk-order-other.note: Only dlv:rowMajor and dlv:columnMajor; any other order is refused at load.

hel-ext-text.note: The HEL extension group text, implemented in full.

hel-ext-temporal.note: The HEL extension group temporal, implemented in full.

hel-ext-quantifier.note: The HEL extension group quantifiers, implemented in full.

hel-ext-geometry.note: The HEL extension group geometry, implemented in full.

hel-ext-register.note: The HEL extension group register, implemented in full.

writer.note: The Writer conformance target, claimed on the evidence the suite defines for it: the engine's Metawriter passes every case of the Writer class of the processor conformance suite (specification/conformance/writer/), run by the engine's own suite runner and, through its hexplain-write command, by run_suite.py --w-cmd; the implementation report of the current suite published under specification/conformance/reports/hexplain-tools/ (suite digest 665b443c5f01, engine commit 1d3df9ad) lists the class with all 88 of its cases passing, and the engine passes the suite's round-trip mode (run_suite.py --round-trip with hexplain-write and hexplain-parse: 247 of the 249 trees, the other two needing the unclaimed chunk features). A text container, a tree document and a chunk table are refused with Unsupported feature, as the serialisation rules require, and so is a field written through a codec whose contract defines no encode direction. Generated Kotlin writers follow the same rules or refuse; the claim is the Metawriter's.

codecs.note: Every codec the engine runs, by the local name of its register IRI; modules names the module that ships each: core holds the minimum codec set, and the codecs-lz, codecs-xz, codecs-tiff, codecs-image and codecs-array plugins the rest. A deployment claims the codecs of the plugins it puts on the class path; `--version` and `hexplain-codec list` print them. Every codec passes its specification vectors when the engine is built. The engine's former identifiers (tiff-lzw, lz4-frame, zstd, xz, ...) are deprecated aliases of these IRIs.
codecs.parameters: Codec parameters are literals of their contract's type (hexplain:parameterValue: integer, boolean, string, bytes, IRI, float, or an rdf:List of these), checked against each codec's contract when a description is loaded. Parameter expressions (hexplain:parameterExpression), run-time codec selection (hexplain:codecFromExpression, every candidate checked and kinds checked per candidate) and hexplain:codecSessionScope are checked when the description is loaded, and a parse runs them: each expression and selection is evaluated in the field's struct each time its step runs, before any codec runs, and a session-keeping codec gets a session per step for the struct instance (bddo:PerInstance), for the parse (bddo:PerLayout) or, without a scope, for each decode; the scope is ignored where no codec of the field keeps a session. A selection value names a candidate by its full IRI or by its local name, and a local name two candidates share names neither. A write runs them the same way, evaluating each expression and selection over the values being written before any codec runs; a selected codec that only decodes is refused with Unsupported feature, and every encode starts afresh (no session-keeping codec encodes). The HDL compiler writes all three from text and YAML: typed and expression arguments, `@codec switch` (a selection whose value is the arm's codec IRI) and `@codec-session`. Generated Kotlin code (hxc) supports all three: it evaluates each expression and selection where the engine does and checks it against the contract as the engine does, keeps sessions per struct instance or per read, bounds each encode step by the writer's output limit, and runs codecs outside the runtime's minimum set through the rt-codecs-* runtime plugins it lists. Generated Kotlin readers and writers preserve integer literal settings on supported byte fields.

encodings.note: Every registered bddo:Encoding, by local name: the five every Physical Parser decodes (utf8, ascii, latin1, utf16le, utf16be) and the twelve further encodings, which a claims statement lists by IRI in its `encodings` member (Processing Model, Further encodings). The engine decodes them through its Java runtime's character sets (FieldFacetCompilers.kt, encodingCharsets), with its own UCS-2 decoders; ebcdic037 (IBM037) and shiftJis (Shift_JIS) are in the JDK's jdk.charsets module, and on a runtime image built without that module the engine refuses them with Unsupported feature when the description is loaded, as the Processing Model requires, and a deployment's claims statement then omits them. A bddo:CustomEncoding is decoded when the runtime has a decoder for its bddo:ianaCharset.

limits.note: Defaults; every one is configurable. helNestingDepth may be raised to 4096.
